summary:
Orbitwell is a crew-health self-assessment prototype for long-duration space missions. It lets astronauts record practical indicators—including resting heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep, and mood—and view clear status cues and trends over time. Short explanations and wellness guidance help crew members understand what their measurements may indicate and when to follow mission medical protocols or contact a flight surgeon.

The project addresses the challenge of monitoring health when distance from Earth, isolation, altered gravity, and other spaceflight hazards can affect physical and mental wellbeing. Making routine measurements easier to interpret could help crews notice changes earlier and communicate them more clearly to medical teams. Orbitwell is a prototype, not certified flight software or a substitute for professional care. AI tools assisted with code, written content, and vector visuals; example health data are synthetic.
details:
Project Details

Orbitwell is a web-based prototype exploring how astronaut crews could review wellness information in a mission-aware dashboard. Users can select a crew member and mission, view a health snapshot, complete a daily check-in, and explore trends over time. The dashboard includes sample views for heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep, and mood. Its readings and crew profiles are fictional demonstration data.

Benefits and intended impact:

Orbitwell brings several types of wellness information into one organized interface, with readings and check-ins associated with a selected crew member and mission. The prototype is intended to spark discussion about making crew wellness information easier to review and follow over time. It is not a medical device, does not provide medical advice, and must not be used for diagnosis or treatment.

Tools and technologies:

We built the project as a browser-based application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Node.js and Express on the server and SQLite for data storage. The interface uses charts and responsive layouts to present information on desktop and mobile. No specialized hardware is required.

What makes it creative:

Orbitwell adapts familiar health-dashboard and mission-operations ideas to a spaceflight setting. Crew and mission selection changes the context of the dashboard, helping demonstrate how wellness records might be organized around a crew’s mission.

Factors considered:

We prioritized readable layouts, clear trends, responsive design, and the relationship between a crew member and their mission. Because health information is sensitive, we also considered the importance of clear limitations: all displayed data and personas are fake, and the prototype is for demonstration only. Orbitwell was created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge in Cincinnati; it is a challenge project and is not an official NASA medical system.
